podcast.body: A classic Bowie hit that, along with "Let's Dance" and "Changes," took up more than half of the Rock charts' top 20 the week of his death in January 2016, indicating its enduring popularity. "Bowie songs took up more than half of the Rock charts top 20, including such classics as Let's Dance, Changes and Life on Mars."

podcast.body: Composed on piano after Bowie's 1971 US tour, this song, alongside "Changes," featured the pomp of glam rock and the poignancy of traditional American pop. It appeared on his late 1971 album 'Hunky Dory', which was his debut on the RCA label. "These songs, including Life on Mars and Changes, would appear on his late 1971 album, Hunky Dory."

podcast.body: This song was recorded in August 1971 at Trident Studios in the Soho area of London, featuring Rick Wakeman on the 100-year-old Bechstein piano, possibly with microphones placed in the men's bathroom for its unique natural reverb. "Recorded in August 1971 at Triton Studios in the Soho area of London, there's Bowie with life on Mars, with Rick Wakeman playing the 100 year old Beckstein piano."
